messages:
Alice M.: FYI handoff from evening shift. We had a pager earlier for increased 502/5xx observed on egress -> third-party routing (probable upstream throttle). Pager went at ~20:12 UTC, mitigated to degraded at ~20:45. Customer impact: short bursts of failed requests for <1% of traffic; a few enterprise customers reported dropped requests (CS looped in).
Incident Bot: INCIDENT 2026-1379 - elevated 502 rate from egress -> routed alerts to #eng-oncall and paged primary.
Alice M.: What we did so far:
- Flipped fallback routing for region-1 to secondary egress pool (manual route policy applied)
- Scoped canary of retry/timeout changes on the frontend for latency-tolerant calls
- Scaled dedicated egress workers (+30%) to absorb burst
- Opened ticket with partner ops (they acknowledged degraded capacity, investigating).
Ben R.: Thanks, Alice. Current status: traffic stable but error spikes still visible at p95 windows. No customer data loss; retries succeeded for most, but a couple of long-running requests failed permanently.
Charu S.: Noted that the request shaping rule we pushed yesterday may have made the tail worse for some endpoints. I'm reverting the shaping for high-rt endpoints now.
Derek L.: If partner confirms sustained throttle, next step is to enable permanent secondary egress routing and adjust caching TTLs for embeddings endpoints to reduce qps. I left ACs in the runbook.
Alice M.: Runbook links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-fallback (follow section "partial-egress-fallback") and playbook quick checks: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/oncall.
Alice M.: Quick commands I ran (paste for handoff):
```
# check egress LB health
kubectl -n infra get svc egress-lb-region1 -o wide
# observe 502 spikes in envoy
kubectl -n infra logs -l app=envoy --since=2h | grep "502" | head
# apply fallback route
redwoodctl routing apply --policy fallback-region1-secondary --force
```
Ben R.: Current assignments for next shift: I'm primary overnight, Derek is secondary. Charu will be on standby for partner escalations. @SRE Rotation please update rota to show Ben primary until 03/03 07:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:
SRE Rotation: rota updated.
Charu S.: Notes for next: check emb-cache hit rate and embedding-cache eviction stats; I saw ttl churn around the incident window. If eviction >10% persist, consider bumping ttl to 5m for tier-1 keys.
Derek L.: Customer comms: CS drafted an interim note. We should sign off if partner doesn't confirm root cause in 2 hours. Draft link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/2026-1379/comm-draft
Alice M.: Outstanding action items (short):
- [Ben] Keep fallback policy in place for next 2h, monitor for regression windows and increase worker pool if errors resurge.
- [Charu] Revert shaping, monitor emb-cache metrics, adjust TTL if eviction >10%.
- [Derek] Coordinate with partner ops for confirmed timeline + postmortem ownership.
- [Alice] Prep quick rollback plan if fallback routing causes downstream problems.
Ben R.: I'll post 30m status updates here. For immediate triage: check these dashboards -> /dashboards/egress-errors, /dashboards/kv-cache, /dashboards/routing-latency.
Alice M.: Additional context for oncall: throttles originated from partner-side rate-limiter hitting anomalous spike after a batch job from them retried. We have logs pointing to identical user-agent patterns. 
Derek L.: If we need to hard-fail, we have an emergency policy: set client-side short-circuit to 429 for non-critical flows. See runbook section "hard-fail-fallbacks".
Incident Bot: RESOLVED? No - status changed to INVESTIGATING -> DEGRADED.
Ben R.: Last note: Post-incident tasks for morning shift: collect full trace samples for affected requests, gather partner's throttling window timestamps, attach to incident ticket. Also add a regression eval against yesterday's rollout for shaping change.
Alice M.: OK passing to Ben (primary). Thanks all, leaving notes in ticket. :rocket:
